summary: Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (1988, 1998) under George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass. He also studied under traditional teacher P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri from 1978 to 1979.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. Educated at Queens College and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lynn Struve, he served as associate professor at Indiana University (1987–2015).

Ellison Banks Findly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tehran and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1948–1952). In 1967, he became a department head at Heidelberg University.
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indology scholar who served as editor for the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926) and pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, holding later posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal, and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara.

Historian Emi Matsushita earned a BA from Nanzan University, a diploma from the University of East Anglia, and an MA from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts with the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a German scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1826), he became full professor there (1835–1860) before serving as professor of Oriental languages at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1860.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Franz Kielhorn, earning a PhD from Berlin. He held chairs at Kiel University (1909, 1918–1919) and the University of Göttingen (1920).

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller. He held professorial chairs at the University of Bologna (1860), the University of Pisa (~1860–1886), and the University of Padua (~1886–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She joined the faculty of the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.
Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College (~1965–1968) and MIT (~1968–1970). She has held professorships at the University of Cambridge and Harvard University (~2008).

Emmanuel Levinas (1906–1995) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Strasbourg and Freiburg, the latter under Martin Heidegger. He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1961–1967), Fribourg, and the University of Paris (~1973–1979).

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a Bangladeshi scholar of history and Indology who studied at Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he held faculty posts at Kyushu University and Kumamoto University (~1977–1982), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum (~1982–1992).

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University (1972) and later as president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).

Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD in Buddhist Textual Studies at Mahidol University (attested 2021) under doctoral supervisor Giuliano Giustarini and co-supervisors Peter Skilling and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held teaching posts as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1923) and professor at Otani University from 1915.

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and became an honorary professor at Otani University (1949–1976).
